notes.reason: First record: what each seed builds on main at 1a0100cd
seed 0 meshes differently since display tessellation plans (#805), which landed alongside these goldens (#826)

the kernel fixes merged together on 13 October (#838, #839, #841, #855, #856) change what these seeds build: several joins that used to fail now succeed, small volume and area shifts, and shell now refuses seeds 6, 14, 43 and 73 with an offset corner error (seed 14 built before: #897)
#936: a fillet or chamfer of a smooth seam is refused as an invalid pick (no corner to round) instead of as unsupported

the model's body mesh is the reference mesher's again (the display plan's since #805, which moved these seeds rather than the kernel fixes above): they build as they did before #805, and seed 14 builds again (#897)
a fillet that used to be refused as unsupported on seed 64's extruded profile now builds, so the design goes on differently: rounds that meet at corners on curved faces (#851)
#936: fillets and chamfers of smooth seams are refused as invalid picks (rejected) instead of unsupported; nothing else changes

#946: small tools in large bodies are traced at their own scale; seeds 26 and 85 now build, 18, 43, 61, 63 and 71 fail with a different message, 19 builds two fewer faces (its fillet pick is also refused as in #936)
#921 with its grid lines kept to display and export meshes (Booleans mesh as before #921): measured volume and area move by about 1e-6 (seed 94 also as in #936)

a hole placed on a face without a direction drills into that face (it took the direction from any face whose plane passed through the point, the last one found, such as a side of a patterned box standing on the point's plane): the holes on these seeds now go straight in (#950)

the last-resort tool nudge is tried the other way when it fails or leaves sliver faces the operands didn't have: seed 43's join builds and the design runs to the end, 31 and 78 come out with fewer faces (#827, #897)
main's fillet changes since the last record (#926, #949) move seeds 33 and 91: a fillet step builds differently or is picked differently

hole tangent inside a stepped boss: touching sews split zero-thickness curved walls, so a pattern of holes spaced by their diameter (touching) in a stepped body cuts exactly instead of by a tool nudge: 42 builds more faces (the walls split where the holes touch), 51 picks other edges afterwards

corner blends on curved faces (#854): seed 33's last fillet (its second body) is built differently; its display-plan and measured volumes now agree (4442.73 mm³; on main they read 4439.42 and 4443.51)
#952: a hole placed on a face drills into the material; seed 81's hole moves its volume by 0.1 mm³ (area by 0.04 mm²)

Cuts join the straight edges they used to leave split along untouched walls (#1049). Replaying each changed seed's new commands on the build before and after gives the same volume, area and faces at every step, and the same refusals (seeds 2 and 95 end on a cut the old build refuses too), except: seed 94's final join was 1.7 mm³ too large before (the box adds 875 − 2.5 × 97.967 = 630.08 mm³ to 5270.48; now 5900.56, before 5902.27), and seed 71's hole differs only in the coarse measuring mesh (identical at 2e-4 mm). Every other volume change is the generator picking other edges by index for fillets and chamfers, some of which are now accepted; seed 71's join now builds.

#1164: a pattern copy of a box sitting flush on the half-ring's top face (a 27 mm2 contact patch) now joins the ring instead of staying a separate shell, so the later random steps pick different edges and positions

A point at a boundary curve's end is that end in the boolean (#391): seeds 0 and 41 lose a sliver edge (8e-5 mm on seed 41) that a cut left. Seed 0's fillet of its two edges then takes out 10.62 mm³, as its edges do alone (3.11 and 7.40 mm³), where it took 5.86. Seed 39 moves by 0.008 mm³; seed 57's chamfer and pattern come in the other order, its body valid with no edge under 10 µm

#391 after merging main: seed 34's area moves by 0.002 mm² (1086.303472 to 1086.305562, 2e-6 relative); its steps, outcome, volume and face, edge and shell counts are unchanged; the same small kind of move as seed 39's

#1213: a round or chamfer on an edge chain that runs on across a curved seam now builds (it was refused with 'a curved seam where the edge chain turns'). Seed 41's second fillet (three edges, radius 1) was one of those refusals and is now built. Replaying the seed's commands on the build before and after gives the same volume, area, faces and edges after each of steps 1 to 6; step 7, the fillet, is refused before and builds after (5292.19 to 5289.17 mm³, area 7395.26 to 7381.22 mm²); the run then reaches its eight steps one step sooner, so its last step is a cut sphere (5185.22 mm³) where it was a join cylinder (the generator draws its later steps from the new state).

#391 after merging main with #1213: seed 41 now reaches its second fillet (built since #1213), and the end-snap fix again drops a sliver edge the cuts left (94 to 93 edges); its steps, outcome, faces and shells are unchanged, volume moves by 0.005 mm³ (5185.215737 to 5185.221068) and area by 0.0014 mm²
the chamfer bug is on main too, see #1390

#1390: a chamfer of a convex edge that would grow the part is refused (TooLarge). Seed 57's 0.5 mm chamfer on the sphere cut's rim, which grew the part since #391 reordered its steps, is now refused, so the run goes on to its later steps and ends ok (16017.21 mm³, 24 faces)
Seed 83 builds: a shell splits a saddle corner (convex and concave edges in turn) into two corners
seed 15 now cuts around a sealed void

#1490: when the last-resort nudge fails both ways, two more screw axes are tried; seed 63's final box join (its face 0.00005 mm off the half-ring's cut face) now builds instead of being refused with an implausible volume, and the design goes on to its fillet

a prism cut in a column round the tool (prism_local): seed 65's rectangular pattern (step 4, a second half-cylinder groove overlapping the first, in a block with a rounded vertical edge) is now built by the exact 2D route in a column clear of the round, where the B-rep tries left it with split edges. The step's part has the 10 faces, 24 edges and 16 vertices it should (28 edges and 18 vertices before), and its volume is 45145.383 mm³ against 45145.214 (exactly 45145.103, both within the mesh measure); the generator then picks other edges for its step 7 fillet, so the run ends on another design (45143.48 mm³, 15 faces)

Seed 31: #1581 no longer maps a pick on an earlier round's seam to some other nearby edge; the second fillet's selection includes the smooth seam at [2, 27.5, 13.5] beside the first round, which is now refused (no corner to round) instead of silently re-rounding a different edge at 1 mm, so the run goes on to a hole. Seed 83: #1316 was recorded before its branch took in #1495; with #1495's shell (an open face next to a concave edge no longer cuts the wall past it) the shelled part keeps more wall (6217 to 6339 mm3), its edges differ, and the 2.5 mm fillet of the first run is not picked; a later fillet is refused as not supported yet (an end face parallel to the edge)

the 2D route sews a cut whose outline has a point a hair from a segment's end (text-recut): seed 53's shell (step 3, a 2 mm shell of an extruded L with an arc side, opened at the notch's inner face) builds its cavity by the 2D route in 77 ms, where it took the B-rep path (2.4 s) and gave a part 336 mm³ lighter, which a box can't then be intersected with (no result). Its section at mid height is 338.27 mm² (a distance-rule raster of the profile gives 343.7, rounding the cavity's concave corners); the generator then builds the step 4 fillet it refused before, so the run goes on another way (16954.55 mm³, 48 faces)

#726 (#1687): a full revolve of a profile off the axis comes out with its planar faces whole, so the revolved section has fewer faces and edges. The fuzz generator picks edges and faces by index, so from their second step these seeds build different designs. Replaying each new design's commands on main and on this branch: seeds 45, 77 and 94 end the same; in seed 21 a box joined onto the ring's flat top now fuses with it, where main kept two touching shells that a later hole split into two bodies.

#726 (#1718): a partial revolve made as a new body comes out with its planar faces whole, so the revolved section has fewer faces and edges. The fuzz generator picks edges and faces by index, so from their second step these seeds build different designs (seed 24's shell now picks the centroid of a whole 270 deg annulus, which lies in the bore, so it is refused and the run goes on). Replaying each new design's commands on main and on this branch: 12 seeds end the same; in seeds 13 and 26 a box joined onto a flat revolved face now fuses with it (main kept two touching shells that a later step split into two bodies), seed 15's last cylinder join, which main refuses, now builds, and seed 78's cut box no longer leaves 87.5 mm² of extra area (the end cap's); seed 63 refuses the same fillet on both and ends with nearly the same body. Seed 9 now ends ok instead of failing, but its new design ends the same on main. No seed gains a failure.

Current main replay: seed 55 now meshes every face and passes validity; edge-consistent measuring meshes (#1753) change its measured volume from 24741.239331 to 24740.927259 mm3. Seed 71 joins with one fewer redundant face and two fewer edges (19/50); its five steps, successful outcome, volume and area are unchanged within the existing 1e-6 tolerances. Both fixed command sequences were replayed with validity checks after every step.

Seed 20: trace conical cutters against earlier conical cuts at finer unshifted tolerances before coarse copies can leave unusable junctions. The circular pattern and final box cut both build; replayed in the app with no feature errors, unchanged 45 faces/116 edges/one shell, no tool nudge, and volume/spatial guards retained. The finer intersection curves change measured volume by 0.020503 mm3 and area by 0.171629 mm2.

After integrating #1718, replay the regenerated revolved-section recipes on the combined branch: seed 13 has 40 faces/101 edges (one face/two edges fewer), seed 94 has 27 faces/63 edges (one face/two edges more). Both complete fixed command sequences pass validity and volume-direction checks after every step, and two independent golden runs per seed agree exactly. Steps, outcomes, body and shell counts are unchanged; area and volume match within existing 1e-6 relative tolerances (seed 13 volume differs by 0.000002 mm3). Only topology counts are updated. The finer unshifted conical-cut route and its geometry guards remain in place.

#1670 and #1753 (mesh export: twisted ruled faces divided to the chord tolerance, and the faces of an edge sharing its points exactly) change the meshes the kernel's validity and volume checks measure: seed 55's body (a filleted box cut by spheres and patterned) now passes the validity check it failed, and its volume moves by 1.3e-5 relative. Pull requests ran only every 8th seed, so main's full run found it. Recorded from main's CI output (Linux).

#853 recorded seeds 13, 71 and 94 as its own branch built them (13: 40 faces/101 edges, 71: 19/50, 94: 27/63), but with main's kernel they build as before (41/103, 20/52, 26/61), so every full run on main failed on them after #853 landed. This puts back the counts main builds; #853's conical-cut refinement (seed 20) is unchanged. Steps, outcomes, volumes and areas are the same.

#1853 (a part revolve of a profile with an edge on the axis is swept a third of a turn at most per face, so the boolean can intersect its faces): seeds 28 and 95 start with a rectangle on the axis turned half a turn, now two quarter turns. Seed 28 (joined by a cylinder) has more faces for the same shape (5902.1214 -> 5902.1117 mm3, the new faces' meshes). Seed 95's hole into it failed with 'boolean Cut: no result' on the half-turn faces and now builds, so the generator's later picks move. Values from Linux CI.
Independently reproduced on unmodified main 1e984c8e on Windows; the extrusion branch produces the same values. Shared references and tolerances remain unchanged.

Seed 94 independently reproduced on unmodified main c5992386 on Windows after the extrusion rebase: the same steps, outcome and geometry values as the rebased branch. Shared references and tolerances remain unchanged.
